name: H2S ice (an estimated index)
paper: the estimate's inputs: C. and M. Cuthbertson, Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 83 (1910) 171, for H2S's gas dispersion; L. Vegard and L. Sinding-Oserød, Avh. Nor. Vidensk.-Akad. Oslo, Mat.-Naturvidensk. Kl. 1942, 1, as the Crystallography Open Database gives it, entry 1539470, https://www.crystallography.net/cod/1539470.cif, SHA-256 4b8ac2109ea328521f0516ba4c1f22ccdcd93c062024d4a69c8df450aa56dbc2, fetched 2026-10-14, for the cell
source: a Lorentz–Lorenz estimate, not a measurement (decision-r08-t5d rulings 3 and 5): the molar refraction of H2S from its gas dispersion as stated at 273.15 K and 101325 Pa (view/atmosphere/rayleigh.ts's row, Z = 1.0006569652444193), with no increment, since the solid is molecular, over the molar volume of cubic H2S phase I (Fm3̄m) (29.33 cm³ mol⁻¹ from 194.809 Å³ and 4 molecules). The gas dispersion is measured over 486.1–656.3 nm and extrapolated beyond. The one open measurement found, Yarnall and Hudson 2022's n at 670 nm, is of amorphous ice deposited at 19 K, a film less dense than the crystal, not the crystal's visible dispersion; it is the method's third check below. The method's checks on measured solids: Ar from its gas dispersion (Peck and Fisher, J. Opt. Soc. Am. 54 (1964) 1362) at the cell of E. R. Dobbs, B. F. Figgins, G. O. Jones, D. C. Piercey and D. P. Riley, Nature 178 (1956) 483, DOI 10.1038/178483a0, as the Crystallography Open Database gives it, entry 1541541, https://www.crystallography.net/cod/1541541.cif, SHA-256 4ac3ecee395a4f006797f4d74469aa7167deaa78a1c68c1b6c4c0bc17122fd23, fetched 2026-10-14 (a = 5.4 Å, four atoms) gives 1.2842 against Sinnock and Smith 1969's measured 1.2708 at 546.1 nm and 80 K (Phys. Rev. 181, 1297); NH3 ice 1.465 against Martonchik et al. 1984's 1.436 at 550 nm (Appl. Opt. 23, 541); and H2S ice at the density of an amorphous film at 19 K, 0.944 g cm⁻³, 1.439 against the 1.407 Yarnall and Hudson 2022 measure there at 670 nm (Astrophys. J. Lett. 931, L4; CC BY 4.0), each above the measurement. k = 0.
licence: estimated values from cited constants and a crystal cell from the Crystallography Open Database (its entry placed in the public domain by its contributors (the entry's notice)); no data set is copied (decision-r08-t5d ruling 5)
reduction: n = √((1 + 2x) ÷ (1 − x)), with x the gas's molar refraction over the solid's molar volume, evaluated on 380–780 nm every 5 nm to six significant figures; k = 0
standIn: a non-absorbing crystal whose real index is a Lorentz–Lorenz estimate from the gas's dispersion at the crystal's density, since only one wavelength of an amorphous film's index is measured openly, not the crystal's visible dispersion: 1.602 at 380 nm, 1.570 at 550 nm and 1.557 at 780 nm
